Orthostasis, tachycardia, gastroparesis, bladder/sexual dysfunction, hypoglycemia unawareness
Acute isolated nerve deficit; often reversible
Unilateral belt-like burning pain, one truncal dermatome

disorders-of-sex-development.name: Disorders of sex development
disorders-of-sex-development.scope: 46,XY DSD (androgen insensitivity, 5-alpha-reductase deficiency), 46,XX DSD (congenital adrenal hyperplasia), mixed gonadal dysgenesis, ambiguous genitalia, pubertal virilization, karyotyping
disorders-of-sex-development.core: Atypical genital development requires urgent exclusion of salt-wasting CAH, then coordinated chromosomal, hormonal, and anatomic assessment with family-centered counseling.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, consanguinity, inherited steroid/receptor defects; maternal androgen exposure can virilize 46,XX fetuses

rows.label: Clues
items: Atypical genitalia, bilateral nonpalpable gonads, severe hypospadias with undescended testes, primary amenorrhea
★ Vomiting, weight loss, hypotension, **hyponatremia/hyperkalemia** in newborn → salt-wasting crisis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Testicular AMH regresses Müllerian ducts; testosterone supports Wolffian ducts; DHT masculinizes external genitalia
21-hydroxylase deficiency diverts precursors toward androgens while reducing cortisol ± aldosterone

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Electrolytes, glucose, 17-hydroxyprogesterone**, cortisol; salt-wasting may emerge after initially normal examination
★ **Karyotype/rapid sex-chromosome testing + pelvic ultrasound** for uterus and gonads
Testosterone, DHT, LH/FSH, AMH; high testosterone:DHT ratio after hCG supports 5-alpha-reductase deficiency
Confirm with targeted molecular testing; involve pediatric endocrinology, genetics, urology, psychology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected adrenal crisis → **IV hydrocortisone + isotonic saline/dextrose**, without awaiting confirmatory results
Salt-wasting CAH maintenance: hydrocortisone, fludrocortisone, salt supplementation in infancy
Complete AIS: discuss gonadectomy after spontaneous puberty; individualize surveillance; estrogen replacement after removal
Mixed dysgenesis with Y-containing dysgenetic gonads → specialist malignancy-risk assessment, often gonadectomy
Avoid rushed irreversible genital procedures; informed shared decisions include option to defer until patient participation

rows.label: Complications
items: Adrenal crisis, infertility, gonadal tumors, psychosocial distress; hormone deficiency affects bone health

rows.label: Prevention
items: Newborn CAH screening, genetic counseling; educate affected families about stress-dose steroids and emergency injections

rows.label: Mimics
items: Müllerian agenesis: 46,XX, absent uterus, normal pubic hair and ovaries
Isolated hypospadias: typical endocrine function; severe proximal forms still warrant DSD evaluation

table.title: Distinguishing profiles
rows: Undervirilized at birth, virilizes at puberty

drug-eruptions.name: Drug eruptions
drug-eruptions.scope: Morbilliform drug eruption, fixed drug eruption, DRESS syndrome, drug discontinuation, antihistamines, topical corticosteroids
drug-eruptions.core: New medication followed by rash: distinguish uncomplicated delayed hypersensitivity from a systemic reaction requiring admission and organ monitoring.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Antibiotics, sulfonamides, anticonvulsants, allopurinol, NSAIDs; prior sensitization accelerates recurrence
Aminopenicillin exposure during EBV infection often produces an exanthem; not automatically lifelong penicillin allergy

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus common in benign eruptions; uncomplicated disease lacks organ dysfunction
★ **Skin pain, blistering, mucosal erosions, hypotension** → severe reaction; urgent hospital evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: T-cell-mediated delayed hypersensitivity; tissue-resident memory cells explain localized recurrence
DRESS: systemic immune activation, sometimes associated with herpesvirus reactivation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Medication timeline**, including OTC agents and recently stopped drugs; examine entire skin and mucosa
Possible systemic reaction → CBC/differential, AST/ALT, bilirubin, creatinine, urinalysis; trend abnormalities
DRESS: compatible exposure, skin/blood/organ abnormalities; RegiSCAR scoring supports diagnosis
Biopsy when morphology uncertain; no routine rechallenge or skin testing during acute illness

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Discontinue culprit drug**; stop nonessential agents if severe reaction and culprit uncertain
Mild exanthem/localized fixed eruption → **topical triamcinolone**, emollients; cetirizine for itching
★ DRESS with substantial organ injury → **systemic prednisone**, specialist-supervised slow taper over weeks to months
Anaphylaxis features → IM epinephrine; DRESS requires inpatient assessment, not antihistamines alone

rows.label: Complications
items: DRESS: hepatitis/liver failure, nephritis, myocarditis, pneumonitis; relapse after rapid steroid withdrawal
Delayed autoimmune thyroiditis or diabetes → follow-up organ testing for several months
Localized fixed eruption often leaves persistent hyperpigmentation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Document culprit, timing, phenotype, severity; provide written avoidance instructions
After severe reactions: avoid culprit/cross-reactive drugs; uncertain allergy labels → specialist evaluation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Viral exanthem: infectious prodrome/exposures; no convincing drug timeline
SJS/TEN: epidermal necrosis and prominent painful mucositis
Urticaria: migratory wheals, individual lesions disappear within 24 h

table.title: Timing and morphology
rows: Usually 1–2 weeks; long-term use does not exclude
Sharply demarcated dusky plaque; identical site

dyslipidemia.name: Dyslipidemia
dyslipidemia.scope: Lipid screening guidelines, ASCVD risk calculation, statin therapy indications, monitoring response to diet and pharmacotherapy
dyslipidemia.core: Excess atherogenic lipoproteins drive ASCVD; treatment intensity follows established disease, severe LDL elevation, diabetes, and estimated absolute cardiovascular risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Familial disorders, saturated-fat intake, obesity, diabetes, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis
Premature ASCVD family history, CKD, smoking, inflammatory disease increase treatment benefit

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; tendon xanthomas/early corneal arcus suggest familial hypercholesterolemia
Severe triglyceride elevation: eruptive xanthomas, pancreatitis; low HDL alone is not a drug target

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retained apoB-containing particles → arterial inflammation and plaque formation
Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase → hepatic LDL-receptor upregulation
Familial hypercholesterolemia: **defective LDL-receptor uptake** → isolated high LDL, clear plasma; high TG: milky plasma

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Lipid panel from age 19, at least every 5 years**; earlier/more often with risk
Nonfasting panel acceptable; markedly high triglycerides → fasting repeat/secondary-cause evaluation; Lp(a) once/lifetime
★ **PREVENT-ASCVD**, ages 30–79, LDL 70–189 without ASCVD: replaces pooled-cohort equations in 2026 guidance
Uncertain statin decision → coronary calcium; zero insufficient for deferral with diabetes, smoking, strong premature history
High total cholesterol alone → full lipid panel before treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Clinical ASCVD (CAD, stroke, PAD) or **LDL ≥190 mg/dL → high-intensity statin**, no risk calculation required
★ Diabetes age 40–75 → **at least moderate-intensity statin**; multiple risk factors favor high intensity
Above LDL target despite maximal statin → ezetimibe; consider PCSK9 inhibitor or bempedoic acid
Severe triglycerides ≥500 → address causes, diet, consider fenofibrate/prescription omega-3 to reduce pancreatitis risk
Adolescent obesity + moderate LDL → **calorie reduction/lifestyle first**; statin only if severe or persistent

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, stroke, peripheral arterial disease; statins → myalgias, rare rhabdomyolysis, small diabetes-risk increase
Baseline ALT; CK only with symptoms/risk; most lipid-lowering drugs deferred during conception/pregnancy/lactation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Mediterranean-style diet, replace saturated fats, exercise, weight reduction, smoking cessation
★ Recheck lipids **4–12 weeks after diet/drug change**, then every 3–12 months; high despite diet → statin
High intensity lowers LDL ≥50%: atorvastatin 40–80 mg or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypothyroidism: elevated TSH; correct before labeling primary dyslipidemia
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia; treat renal cause

table.title: Risk-based primary prevention and secondary target

eating-disorders.name: Eating disorders
eating-disorders.scope: Anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder, refeeding syndrome, medical complications, hospitalization criteria
eating-disorders.core: Disordered intake or compensatory behaviors require assessment of medical instability, suicidality, and malnutrition at any body size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Adolescence, dieting, weight stigma, perfectionism, trauma; psychiatric comorbidity and family history

rows.label: Clues
items: Restrictive disease: cold intolerance, lanugo, bradycardia, orthostasis, menstrual suppression; amenorrhea not required
Purging: parotid hypertrophy, **raised amylase**, enamel erosion, knuckle calluses; hypokalemic hypochloremic alkalosis
★ **Syncope, arrhythmia, hypothermia or severe electrolyte abnormalities** → urgent stabilization

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Starvation suppresses gonadal axis and reduces cardiac mass; vomiting causes chloride/volume depletion
Refeeding insulin surge shifts phosphate, potassium and magnesium intracellularly

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical interview plus weight trajectory, vitals/orthostatics, **ECG, electrolytes, Mg, phosphate**
Binge: loss of control plus unusually large intake; bulimia/BED require episodes ≥weekly for 3 months
Assess suicide risk, substance use, exercise, laxatives; normal BMI does not exclude severe disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Medical admission for instability: e.g., HR <50, BP <90/60, severe electrolyte disturbance or acute food refusal
★ Refeeding → **thiamine**, nutritional rehabilitation, serial phosphate/K/Mg and cardiac monitoring
Adolescent anorexia → family-based treatment; adults → eating-disorder-focused psychotherapy; medication alone insufficient
Bulimia → CBT plus fluoxetine; avoid bupropion because of seizures
BED → CBT; lisdexamfetamine for selected adults, monitor misuse/cardiovascular risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → osteoporosis, infertility; cardiac failure, arrhythmic death; purging → arrhythmias, esophageal injury
Refeeding → hypophosphatemia, respiratory failure, edema, delirium; high suicide mortality
Severe starvation → **hypoalbuminemia** with pitting edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early recognition of growth/weight-trajectory changes; reduce weight-based stigma; relapse follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperthyroidism: increased appetite with tremor and heat intolerance
GI malabsorption: involuntary weight loss without weight/shape-driven restriction

eating-disorders.evidence: Guideline framework checked 2026-10-30: [APA eating disorders guideline, 2023](https://www.psychiatry.org/psychiatrists/practice/clinical-practice-guidelines/eating-disorders); thresholds: established clinical teaching.

table.title: Diagnostic distinction
rows: Restriction or purging + weight-gain fear/distorted self-image

essential-hypertension.name: Essential hypertension
essential-hypertension.scope: Blood pressure staging, nonpharmacologic interventions (weight loss, DASH, exercise), first-line antihypertensive agents, resistant hypertension
essential-hypertension.core: Persistently elevated arterial pressure usually reflects multifactorial primary hypertension; confirm accurate repeated measurements before long-term treatment decisions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, family history, obesity, excess sodium/alcohol, inactivity, poor sleep
NSAIDs, stimulants, oral contraceptives can raise BP; assess before labeling primary disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; headache alone does not establish hypertensive emergency
★ **Acute target-organ injury** with severe pressure → hypertensive emergency; BP number alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased vascular resistance, altered renal sodium handling, sympathetic/RAAS activation sustain elevated pressure
Chronic endothelial injury accelerates atherosclerosis and small-vessel organ damage
Older adults: large-artery stiffness (low compliance) → **isolated systolic hypertension**, wide pulse pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Average ≥2 readings on ≥2 visits; confirm using **home BP or ambulatory monitoring**
Rest seated, feet supported, correct cuff, arm at heart level; avoid recent caffeine/exercise
BMP, creatinine/eGFR, urinalysis/albuminuria, lipids, glucose/A1c, ECG assess risk and injury
Resistant: above goal on 3 agents including diuretic, or controlled on ≥4; exclude pseudoresistance
Child/adolescent high oscillometric reading → **confirm by auscultation** before ambulatory monitoring or workup

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **DASH diet, weight reduction, sodium restriction, aerobic activity**, moderate alcohol; target generally <130/80
≥140/90 → drugs, usually two classes; ≥130/80 with CVD, diabetes, CKD, or PREVENT ≥7.5% → drugs
★ Low-risk stage 1: **3–6 months lifestyle**, then drugs if still ≥130/80; updated 2025 threshold
Initial: chlorthalidone, amlodipine, lisinopril, or losartan; albuminuric CKD → ACE inhibitor/ARB (older exams: any diabetes)
Resistant after optimized triple regimen → spironolactone; monitor K/creatinine; never combine ACE inhibitor + ARB

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, LV hypertrophy/HF, CKD, retinopathy, aortic disease
Thiazide: low Na/K, gout; ACE inhibitor: cough/angioedema; RAAS drugs contraindicated in pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication adherence, home readings, regular follow-up; assess orthostatic symptoms in older adults
Weight loss: largest lifestyle BP drop, ~1 mm Hg/kg; smoking cessation barely lowers resting BP
BP control: largest modifiable stroke-risk reduction; also prevents concentric LVH and HF

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: office high, home normal
Masked hypertension: elevated out-of-office only; secondary causes: abrupt/refractory pressure with renal/endocrine clues

foodborne-illnesses.name: Foodborne illnesses
foodborne-illnesses.scope: Staphylococcus aureus enterotoxin, Bacillus cereus, Clostridium perfringens, scombroid, ciguatera, Salmonella, Campylobacter
foodborne-illnesses.core: Incubation time and the dominant symptom separate preformed-toxin vomiting from intestinal infection requiring selective stool testing and antibiotics.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Food improperly refrigerated/reheated; shared-meal outbreaks; raw poultry/eggs, unpasteurized dairy, undercooked meat
Infancy, older age, immunosuppression or vascular disease increase invasive Salmonella risk
Improperly chilled tuna/mackerel → scombroid; tropical reef fish → ciguatera

rows.label: Clues
items: Abrupt short-lived emesis without fever favors ingested toxin; inflammatory enteritis → fever or bloody stools
★ **Severe dehydration, bacteremia signs or persistent bloody diarrhea** → urgent assessment
Campylobacter pain may mimic appendicitis; poultry exposure supports both major invasive enteric pathogens
Fish toxins: scombroid → flushing/urticaria; ciguatera → paresthesias, hot/cold temperature reversal

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Ingested enterotoxins act rapidly; scombroid: histamine; ciguatoxin activates voltage-gated sodium channels
Invasive mucosal infection induces inflammation and can permit bloodstream spread
S aureus: **heat-stable** preformed enterotoxin builds in unrefrigerated food; cooking does not destroy it

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Mild brief outbreak illness → **clinical diagnosis**, usually no stool studies
Fever, bloody/mucoid stool, severe tenderness or sepsis → stool PCR/culture including Shiga toxin testing
Suspected bacteremia → blood cultures; report suspected outbreaks to public health

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Scombroid → **diphenhydramine/famotidine**; anaphylaxis → epinephrine; ciguatera → supportive care
Oral rehydration; severe dehydration → IV isotonic fluids; toxin syndromes do not benefit from antibiotics
Campylobacter severe/prolonged or high-risk illness → azithromycin; most mild cases resolve untreated
Nontyphoidal Salmonella: severe/invasive or high-risk host → ceftriaxone or susceptibility-directed antibiotic
★ Suspected **STEC → avoid antibiotics and antimotility drugs**; hemolytic uremic syndrome risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Campylobacter → Guillain-Barré, reactive arthritis; Salmonella → bacteremia, vascular infection, sickle-cell osteomyelitis
Volume depletion → AKI; antibiotics may prolong uncomplicated Salmonella carriage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Cook poultry/eggs thoroughly; separate raw foods, rapid refrigeration, handwashing; avoid unpasteurized products

rows.label: Mimics
items: Norovirus: contagious outbreak with vomiting and diarrhea
Appendicitis: focal progressive peritoneal findings; toxin illness usually self-limited

foodborne-illnesses.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [CDC marine toxins](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/environmental-hazards-risks/food-poisoning-from-marine-toxins.html), CDC Salmonella/Campylobacter and IDSA infectious-diarrhea guidance.

table.title: Timing after exposure
rows: Vomiting; cream pastries, mayonnaise salads, handled meats

generalized-anxiety-disorder.name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
generalized-anxiety-disorder.scope: GAD diagnostic criteria, pharmacotherapy (SSRIs, SNRIs, buspirone), psychotherapy (CBT), differential diagnosis
generalized-anxiety-disorder.core: Difficult-to-control worry about multiple everyday domains on most days for at least 6 months causes distress or functional impairment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family anxiety history, chronic stress, trauma, female sex, comorbid depression
Caffeine, stimulants, thyroid hormone excess, and substance withdrawal can reproduce symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Adults: **≥3** of restlessness, fatigue, poor concentration, irritability, muscle tension, sleep disturbance
Children require only one associated symptom; reassurance provides limited sustained relief
Worries shift among health, family, work, and finances rather than one circumscribed trigger
Assess suicidality, substance use, depressive symptoms, and manic history before treatment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Heightened threat appraisal and impaired fear regulation perpetuate autonomic arousal and anticipatory worry
Avoidance and reassurance-seeking reinforce anxiety, providing targets for cognitive and behavioral interventions

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis** after excluding substance effects and medical explanations
GAD-7 quantifies severity and response; not a substitute for diagnostic interview
TSH, ECG, or other testing guided by tremor, weight change, palpitations, or examination
Symptoms confined to another disorder, such as obsessions or trauma reminders, favor that diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **CBT** targets cognitive distortions, avoidance, and worry; exercise and sleep regularity support recovery
★ Persistent impairment → **SSRI** such as escitalopram/sertraline, or SNRI such as venlafaxine/duloxetine
Buspirone: scheduled nonbenzodiazepine option; delayed onset, low dependence risk, not useful as needed
Allow several weeks at therapeutic dose; continue effective treatment after remission, then taper gradually
Benzodiazepines: brief selected bridging only; avoid chronic use, especially with opioids or fall risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Depression, impaired function, substance misuse; benzodiazepine dependence and withdrawal
SSRIs/SNRIs: GI effects, sexual dysfunction, early activation; SNRIs may increase BP

rows.label: Prevention
items: Reduce caffeine/stimulants, practice CBT skills, monitor relapse during medication taper
Address chronic stress and comorbid sleep, mood, or substance-use disorders

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic disorder: discrete abrupt attacks with anticipatory fear
Adjustment disorder: stressor-linked symptoms beginning within 3 months
Hyperthyroidism: heat intolerance, weight loss, tremor, suppressed TSH

generalized-anxiety-disorder.evidence: Not checked online; established psychiatric diagnostic and treatment teaching.

gestational-diabetes-mellitus.name: Gestational diabetes mellitus
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Screening (50g oral glucose challenge at 24-28 weeks), diagnostic 3-hour 100g test, glycemic targets, nutritional therapy, insulin, fetal and neonatal complications (macrosomia, hypoglycemia, RDS, polycythemia)
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.core: Pregnancy-induced insulin resistance unmasks hyperglycemia, increasing fetal insulin secretion and growth; screen routinely at 24–28 weeks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, prior GDM/macrosomia, family history of type 2 diabetes, PCOS
High-risk patients need early assessment for previously unrecognized overt diabetes

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; excessive fetal growth or polyhydramnios may prompt evaluation
Early marked hyperglycemia suggests preexisting diabetes rather than typical later-onset GDM

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental hormones increase maternal insulin requirements; inadequate beta-cell compensation causes dysglycemia
Maternal glucose crosses placenta; insulin does not; fetal hyperinsulinemia persists briefly after birth
Fetal hyperinsulinemia → macrosomia; antagonizes cortisol → less surfactant, **RDS**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Two-step screen: **nonfasting 50 g challenge**, 1-hour threshold 130–140 mg/dL by local protocol
Positive challenge → fasting 100 g, 3-hour OGTT; **≥2 abnormal values** diagnose GDM
Alternative one-step 75 g OGTT: fasting ≥92, 1-hour ≥180, or 2-hour ≥153 mg/dL
HbA1c alone does not replace pregnancy glucose testing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First: **individualized nutrition, activity, home glucose monitoring**; avoid severe carbohydrate restriction
★ Targets: fasting **<95**, 1-hour <140, or 2-hour <120 mg/dL
Above targets despite lifestyle → **insulin preferred**; metformin crosses placenta, counsel if used
Medication need or poor control → fetal surveillance; delivery timing depends on control and obstetric findings
Suspected fetal weight ≥4,500 g with diabetes → discuss planned cesarean

rows.label: Complications
items: Maternal: preeclampsia, cesarean delivery, future type 2 diabetes
Fetal: macrosomia, shoulder dystocia, birth trauma; poor control increases stillbirth risk
Neonate: **hypoglycemia**, RDS, polycythemia, jaundice; congenital anomalies mainly reflect pregestational diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Postpartum **75 g OGTT at 4–12 weeks**; lifelong diabetes testing every 1–3 years
Breastfeeding, weight management, activity; most GDM insulin needs resolve after placental delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pregestational diabetes: overt diagnostic-range hyperglycemia early in pregnancy
Physiologic glycosuria: lower renal threshold without diagnostic blood glucose abnormalities

health-care-law-and-malpractice.name: Health care law and malpractice
health-care-law-and-malpractice.scope: EMTALA, medical malpractice elements (duty, breach, causation, damages), patient abandonment and dismissal, Good Samaritan laws, tort liability
health-care-law-and-malpractice.core: Malpractice is a civil tort requiring duty, breach, actual and proximate causation, and damages.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ Professional duty usually arises from an established **clinician–patient relationship**
Breach measured against a reasonably prudent clinician under similar circumstances
Employer may share liability for employees acting within scope of employment

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Medicare ED → **medical screening exam**, stabilize emergencies. Labor → delivery including placenta
Transfer → reduce risk, confirm capable facility accepts, send records, arrange qualified transport
★ Dismissal → advance written notice, interim care, referral assistance and records transfer

rows.label: Don't
items: ★ Never delay screening or stabilization for payment or insurance verification
Abandonment → unilateral withdrawal while ongoing care needed, before reasonable transition

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Unstable transfer → informed written request or physician certification of net benefit
Good Samaritan statutes → protection for **good-faith volunteer emergency aid**, varying by state
Gross negligence or willful misconduct generally outside Good Samaritan protection

rows.label: Traps
items: Known complication despite reasonable care ≠ breach
Nonconsensual procedure without emergency justification → possible **battery**, an intentional tort

health-care-law-and-malpractice.evidence: Checked CMS, 42 USC §1395dd, AMA dismissal ethics, Mich. Comp. Laws §691.1501 and Cornell LII, Nov 2026.

hematuria.name: Hematuria
hematuria.scope: Microscopic hematuria, gross hematuria, dipstick confirmation with urine sediment, glomerular vs extraglomerular workup, cystoscopy and CT urography indications
hematuria.core: Urinary RBCs require localization to glomerular versus urologic bleeding, then malignancy evaluation based on risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Urothelial cancer: older age, smoking, aromatic amines, pelvic radiation, cyclophosphamide

rows.label: Clues
items: Clots favor urologic bleeding; edema and hypertension suggest nephritis
★ Painless visible bleeding → malignancy concern even if transient
Colicky flank pain suggests stone; dysuria and urgency favor infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Glomerular capillary injury permits RBC passage; tubular transit distorts RBCs and forms casts

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Positive dipstick → **urine microscopy**; ≥3 RBC/hpf on properly collected specimen defines microhematuria
★ RBC casts, dysmorphic RBCs, proteinuria or renal dysfunction → nephrology plus risk-based urologic evaluation
★ Unexplained gross bleeding → **cystoscopy + CT urography**; MR urography if contrast CT contraindicated
Assess age, sex, smoking, RBC count and gross bleeding history; anticoagulation does not change evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: UTI → antibiotics, then repeat microscopy after resolution; persistent RBCs → risk-stratified workup
Clot retention → large-bore three-way Foley, irrigation, urgent urology

rows.label: Complications
items: Obstructive AKI from clots; anemia with sustained bleeding

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation to reduce future urothelial cancer risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Myoglobinuria or hemoglobinuria: positive heme with absent RBCs
Food or phenazopyridine discoloration: red urine with negative heme

table.title: Microscopic hematuria workup by malignancy risk
rows: Same anatomic workup as gross bleeding

herpes-zoster.name: Herpes zoster
herpes-zoster.scope: Varicella zoster reactivation, dermatomal rash, herpes zoster ophthalmicus, Ramsay Hunt syndrome, oral antivirals, postherpetic neuralgia, Shingrix vaccine
herpes-zoster.core: Latent varicella-zoster reactivation causes painful unilateral dermatomal vesicles; ophthalmic involvement or disseminated disease changes urgency and treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, HIV, malignancy, transplantation, immunosuppressive drugs
Previous chickenpox or live varicella vaccination establishes latency; no new exposure required

rows.label: Clues
items: Burning/allodynia can precede eruption by days; crops crust over approximately 7–10 days
★ **V1 distribution, nasal-tip lesions, eye pain** → urgent ophthalmology for zoster ophthalmicus
★ **Ear vesicles + ipsilateral facial paralysis** ± hearing/vestibular symptoms → Ramsay Hunt syndrome
Multiple noncontiguous dermatomes or >20 lesions outside primary/adjacent dermatomes suggests dissemination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced VZV-specific cellular immunity permits virus to travel from sensory ganglion to skin
Neuronal inflammation/injury explains acute pain and persistent neuropathic symptoms

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical eruption → **clinical diagnosis**; atypical lesions → vesicle-base VZV PCR
Assess ocular, neurologic, and systemic findings; consider immunodeficiency evaluation for unusually severe/recurrent disease
CSF PCR for suspected CNS infection; do not delay treatment in high-risk presentations

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Valacyclovir, famciclovir, or acyclovir** ideally within 72 hours; still treat new lesions or complications
Dissemination, visceral/CNS disease, severe immunosuppression → **IV acyclovir**
Acute pain: acetaminophen/NSAID, add neuropathic agent when needed; avoid routine systemic steroids
Ramsay Hunt: antiviral plus glucocorticoid early; eye lubrication/protection for incomplete closure
Postherpetic neuralgia: **gabapentin**/pregabalin, lidocaine patch; TCA anticholinergic in elderly; no late antiviral

rows.label: Complications
items: Persistent pain >90 days, secondary bacterial infection, corneal injury, vision loss
Meningoencephalitis, vasculopathy, visceral spread in vulnerable patients

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Shingrix two doses** for adults ≥50 years or immunocompromised ≥19 years, including prior zoster
Cover lesions, **avoid susceptible contacts** until crusted; exposure causes chickenpox, not immediate shingles
Disseminated: airborne/contact until crusted; immunocompromised localized: same precautions until dissemination excluded

rows.label: Mimics
items: HSV: recurrent localized lesions, often oral/genital rather than a full dermatome
Contact dermatitis: prominent itch, exposure pattern, no neuropathic prodrome

hip-fractures.name: Hip fractures
hip-fractures.scope: Femoral neck fracture, intertrochanteric fracture, avascular necrosis, preoperative stabilization, surgical repair
hip-fractures.core: An older adult unable to bear weight after a fall may have a hip fracture even when initial radiographs are normal.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Osteoporosis, frailty, prior fragility fracture, impaired vision/balance, sedatives
Young adults: high-energy trauma; consider pathologic fracture when mechanism is minimal and imaging atypical

rows.label: Clues
items: Groin/hip pain, pain with passive rotation or axial loading
★ Displaced injury: **shortened, externally rotated leg**; impacted fractures may allow some walking
Assess distal perfusion, neurologic function, other trauma; document preinjury mobility and cognition

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Intracapsular displacement can disrupt retinacular branches of medial circumflex femoral artery
Extracapsular region has better blood supply but can bleed substantially into surrounding tissues

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **AP pelvis + lateral hip radiographs**; avoid forceful frog-leg positioning in suspected fracture
★ Persistent suspicion with negative x-ray → **MRI**; CT if MRI unavailable/contraindicated
CBC, electrolytes, renal function, ECG, type/screen; assess anticoagulant use and reversible medical instability

rows.label: Tx
items: Analgesia, consider fascia iliaca block; IV fluids for depletion, pressure protection
★ **Repair within 24–48 hours** after correcting major instability; avoid unnecessary testing delays
Reverse relevant anticoagulation for surgery; perioperative antibiotics and pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis when safe
Early weight bearing/mobilization, PT/OT, delirium prevention; orthogeriatric co-management improves recovery
Nonoperative care reserved for selected palliative situations after goals-of-care discussion

rows.label: Complications
items: Femoral neck: avascular necrosis, nonunion; intertrochanteric: blood loss
VTE, delirium, pneumonia, pressure injury, loss of independence, increased mortality
Arthroplasty: dislocation/infection; monitor postoperative neurovascular status and wound

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Fragility fracture → **osteoporosis treatment**, adequate calcium/vitamin D, fall-risk reduction
Medication review, balance/strength training, home safety and assistive device assessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Posterior hip dislocation: dashboard; flexed, adducted, **internally rotated**, short leg; sciatic injury; urgent reduction
Greater trochanteric pain: lateral tenderness, generally preserved weight bearing
Pelvic insufficiency fracture: sacral/pelvic pain, may require MRI

table.title: Definitive repair
rows: Sliding hip screw or cephalomedullary nail

hiv-infection.name: HIV infection
hiv-infection.scope: Acute HIV, testing, ART start, opportunistic infection prophylaxis, PrEP/PEP, opportunistic infections (CMV retinitis, toxoplasmosis, PJP)
hiv-infection.core: HIV progressively depletes CD4 cells; early diagnosis and suppressive ART prevent immune failure and sexual transmission.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual exposure, shared injection equipment, perinatal transmission; other STIs increase acquisition risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Acute infection 2–4 weeks post-exposure: fever, rash, sore throat, **mucosal ulcers**, diarrhea, generalized lymphadenopathy
Weight loss, thrush, recurrent candida/herpes, **extensive adult molluscum** → test HIV; dysphagia → candidal esophagitis
Child/teen: chronic fever/diarrhea, poor growth, generalized nodes, splenomegaly, **polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retroviral integration creates lifelong reservoirs; ongoing replication drives immune depletion and inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Fourth-generation Ag/Ab → HIV-1/2 differentiation assay**; discordance → HIV RNA
★ Recent exposure/acute syndrome despite negative screen → **HIV RNA**, before antibodies appear
Baseline viral load, CD4, genotype, renal/liver function, HBV/HCV/TB, pregnancy testing, **cervical cytology**
AIDS: CD4 <200 or AIDS-defining illness regardless of count
Prenatal: opt-out screening; refusal → counsel, re-offer later; never test without consent

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Start **integrase-based ART promptly**, usually bictegravir/TAF/emtricitabine; assess HBV coinfection and interactions
Do not delay routine ART for genotype; cryptococcal/TB meningitis require disease-specific deferred timing
PJP: TMP-SMX; add glucocorticoid if PaO₂ <70 or A–a gradient ≥35
Toxoplasmosis: **pyrimethamine/sulfadiazine/leucovorin**, else TMP-SMX; CMV retinitis: valganciclovir, ophthalmology
Untreated/viremic mother's newborn → **triple ART** ASAP, ideally within 6 h, ≤6 weeks; suppressed mother → zidovudine alone

rows.label: Complications
items: Opportunistic infections, malignancies, wasting, neurocognitive disease, kidney disease
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome after ART; drug toxicity/interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ PJP prophylaxis: **TMP-SMX** with CD4 <200 before/starting ART; on ART, <100 or 100–200 with viremia
Toxoplasma IgG positive + CD4 <100 → prophylaxis; MAC <50 only without immediate effective ART
★ Exposure ≤72 hours → **28-day PEP: dolutegravir + TDF/emtricitabine**; do not delay for laboratory results
PrEP: TDF/emtricitabine, cabotegravir, or lenacapavir; exclude HIV first, continue serial testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: EBV mononucleosis: atypical lymphocytes, heterophile positivity; acute HIV can be heterophile-negative
Primary CNS lymphoma: often solitary lesion; biopsy after failed empiric anti-Toxoplasma treatment, earlier if serology/imaging/CSF PCR disagree
SCID/CVID: low immunoglobulins; SCID lymphopenia, no nodes; perinatal HIV: PJP, thrush, nodes, normal lymphocytes

table.title: Advanced-disease syndromes
rows: Dry cough, hypoxemia, ground-glass; sputum/BAL silver stain
Ring-enhancing mass lesions, edema/mass effect; positive IgG
Cognitive decline; non-enhancing subcortical demyelination, no mass effect

hyperbilirubinemia.name: Hyperbilirubinemia
hyperbilirubinemia.scope: Gilbert syndrome, Crigler-Najjar, Dubin-Johnson, Rotor, unconjugated vs conjugated, biliary atresia
hyperbilirubinemia.core: Fractionate bilirubin first: indirect elevation reflects production or conjugation problems; direct elevation requires assessment of hepatobiliary excretion.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Fasting, illness or dehydration triggers Gilbert jaundice; family history suggests inherited bilirubin disorders
Persistent infant jaundice can reflect biliary atresia even after initially reassuring appearance

rows.label: Clues
items: Indirect bilirubin is albumin-bound and absent from urine; direct bilirubin can darken urine
★ Infant **pale/acholic stools**, dark urine, hepatomegaly → obstructive cholestasis
Pruritus, pale stools and elevated alkaline phosphatase suggest impaired bile flow
Severe neonatal indirect elevation with lethargy, poor feeding or abnormal tone → bilirubin neurotoxicity

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Heme breakdown yields unconjugated pigment; hepatic UGT conjugation enables biliary elimination
Unbound unconjugated bilirubin crosses the immature blood–brain barrier; conjugated bilirubin does not cause kernicterus
Large hematoma/cephalhematoma resorption → bilirubin overproduction, indirect jaundice

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Total/direct bilirubin**, AST/ALT, alkaline phosphatase/GGT; CBC/reticulocytes/LDH for suspected hemolysis
Isolated mild indirect elevation with normal liver tests and no hemolysis → Gilbert diagnosis
★ Jaundice beyond 2 weeks → fractionate; **direct ≥1 mg/dL at 2–4 weeks** → urgent referral
Infant cholestasis → ultrasound; biliary atresia assessment may require biopsy and operative cholangiography
Adult conjugated elevation with pain/obstruction → RUQ ultrasound before advanced duct imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected biliary atresia → urgent pediatric hepatology/surgery; **early Kasai portoenterostomy**
Severe neonatal indirect, even Coombs-positive → **phototherapy** first; exchange: failure, critical level, encephalopathy
Crigler–Najjar I → intensive phototherapy, definitive liver transplant; type II responds to phenobarbital
Gilbert, Dubin–Johnson and Rotor → reassurance once competing pathology excluded
Cholestasis → nutritional support, fat-soluble vitamins and cause-specific treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Indirect neonatal hyperbilirubinemia → acute encephalopathy/kernicterus
Untreated atresia → cirrhosis, portal hypertension, liver failure

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Inspect stool color and fractionate persistent infant jaundice; never label conjugated jaundice physiologic

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hemolysis: anemia, reticulocytosis, low haptoglobin; newborn ABO: mother O, baby A/B, Coombs-positive
Choledochal cyst: cystic/dilated extrahepatic ducts on ultrasound
Physiologic jaundice: indirect, after 24 h, peaks days 3–5, thriving; transient UGT immaturity
Breast-milk jaundice: indirect, thriving; direct elevation excludes it

hyperbilirubinemia.evidence: Infant referral checked 2026-10-30: [AAP 2025](https://publications.aap.org/aapnews/news/pdfDownload/31302); inherited syndromes established teaching.

hyperthyroidism.name: Hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis
hyperthyroidism.scope: Graves disease, toxic multinodular goiter, toxic adenoma, subacute thyroiditis, thyroid storm, beta-blockers, thionamides, radioactive iodine
hyperthyroidism.core: Excess circulating thyroid hormone → heat intolerance, weight loss despite appetite, tremor, and tachycardia; hormone overproduction differs from destructive release.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune history, female sex; older age favors autonomous nodules
Iodine load, amiodarone, exogenous thyroid hormone; infection/surgery can precipitate storm

rows.label: Clues
items: Hyperreflexia, lid lag, onycholysis, frequent stools, proximal weakness, widened pulse pressure; older adults: apathetic
★ **Thyroid storm**: fever, delirium, severe tachyarrhythmia, vomiting, heart failure; clinical diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased tissue metabolic activity and beta-adrenergic sensitivity explain systemic manifestations
Thionamides block thyroid peroxidase; PTU also reduces peripheral T4 → T3 conversion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TSH first → free T4**, total T3 if T4 normal; suppressed TSH with elevated hormones
TRAb establishes Graves; uncertain cause → **Doppler ultrasound** or radioiodine uptake (not if pregnant/lactating)
Low uptake: thyroiditis/exogenous hormone; low thyroglobulin supports exogenous ingestion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptom control: **propranolol**; caution in asthma or decompensated HF
★ Storm → ICU, cooling/fluids, beta-blockade if tolerated, **PTU → iodine ≥1 hour later**, hydrocortisone
Radioiodine contraindicated during pregnancy/lactation; significant active orbitopathy favors another definitive treatment
Compression/suspicious nodule → thyroidectomy after control; pregnancy: first-trimester PTU, later methimazole

rows.label: Complications
items: AF, embolism, osteoporosis, mild hypercalcemia, cardiomyopathy; radioiodine often → hypothyroidism
★ Thionamides: **fever/sore throat → stop drug, urgent CBC**; PTU → severe hepatotoxicity
Pregnancy: thionamides/TRAb cross placenta → **fetal goiter**, impaired swallowing, polyhydramnios

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor free T4 early during treatment; TSH recovery lags
Smoking cessation for orbitopathy; definitive treatment before planned pregnancy when feasible

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic disorder: episodic symptoms without thyroid biochemical abnormalities
Pheochromocytoma: paroxysmal headache, sweating, severe hypertension
Menopause: hot flashes with menstrual transition, normal thyroid testing
Orbital pseudotumor: involves muscle bellies and tendons; Graves spares tendons

table.title: Etiology determines treatment
rows: Diffuse uptake; bruit, orbitopathy, pretibial myxedema, acropachy (clubbing)
One hot nodule, suppressed surrounding tissue
NSAID; prednisone if severe; no thionamides

hypothermia-and-frostbite.name: Hypothermia and frostbite
hypothermia-and-frostbite.scope: Accidental hypothermia, core rewarming techniques, frostbite stages, rapid warm water bath rewarming, delayed surgical debridement
hypothermia-and-frostbite.core: Cold exposure can cause systemic core-temperature depression and local freezing injury; stabilize the patient before thawing threatened tissue.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Wet/windy exposure, homelessness, alcohol/drugs, extremes of age, immobility
Hypothyroidism, hypoglycemia, sepsis, malnutrition; frostbite risk rises with tight boots and vascular disease

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Core temperature <35°C** defines hypothermia; use low-reading core thermometer
Shivering, slowed cognition → later bradycardia, hypoventilation, absent shivering, coma
ECG: Osborn J waves; severe disease predisposes to ventricular arrhythmia
Frozen tissue: pale, waxy, hard, insensate; after thaw, blister characteristics help estimate depth

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Heat loss exceeds production → enzyme, cardiac, and CNS dysfunction
Local ice crystals and endothelial injury cause microvascular thrombosis; refreezing greatly worsens damage

rows.label: Dx
items: ABCs, core temperature, bedside glucose, ECG; evaluate electrolytes, renal function, trauma, intoxication
Check pulse/breathing carefully because rates can be extremely slow; monitor continuously
Deep frostbite: specialist perfusion imaging helps salvage/prognosis after rewarming, not before stabilization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Remove wet clothes, insulate, **gentle handling**; warm trunk before limbs, avoid rough movement
★ **32–35°C, alert** → insulation/external heat; <32°C → **active external + internal rewarming**
Warmed IV fluids prevent further cooling; severe instability/arrest → extracorporeal rewarming when available
★ Frostbite: **37–39°C circulating water** until thawed, only when refreezing can be prevented
Analgesia, loose dressings, separate digits, tetanus update; deep injury → urgent thrombolysis/iloprost evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Afterdrop, hypotension, dysrhythmia, rhabdomyolysis; tissue loss, neuropathic pain, cold sensitivity
★ After rewarming severe frostbite → **admit**, wound care; **delay amputation until demarcation** unless infected/septic
No rubbing, direct dry heat, or walking on thawed feet when avoidable; prophylactic antibiotics not routine

rows.label: Prevention
items: Dry layered insulation, warm shelter, buddy checks, adequate food; avoid alcohol in cold exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonfreezing trench foot: prolonged wet exposure without tissue freezing
Raynaud phenomenon: episodic reversible vasospasm without frozen tissue

hypothermia-and-frostbite.evidence: Frostbite guidance checked 2026-10-30: [WMS 2024](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/10806032231222359); hypothermia content established teaching.

hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.name: Hypothesis testing and statistical tests
hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.scope: Null and alternative hypotheses, Type I and Type II errors, statistical power, confidence intervals, p-values, t-tests (paired, unpaired), ANOVA, chi-square, Pearson correlation
hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.core: Hypothesis tests quantify incompatibility with a null model; confidence intervals describe effect estimates and uncertainty.

rows.label: Definition
items: H0: no difference/association; H1: specified difference or association
★ **α**: false-positive probability; Type I error rejects a true null
★ **β**: false-negative probability; Type II error misses a real effect

rows.label: Formula
items: Power = **1 − β**; increases with sample size, effect size, α, lower variability
95% CI ≈ estimate ± 1.96 × standard error; plausible range for true effect

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **p-value**: probability of equally/more extreme data assuming H0; not probability H0 true
95% CI excludes 0 for differences or 1 for ratios → two-sided p <0.05

rows.label: Use when
items: Pearson r: linear association between continuous variables; range −1 to +1
Ordinal/non-normal independent data → Mann–Whitney; paired → Wilcoxon signed-rank

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Nonsignificant ≠ equivalent; statistical significance ≠ clinical importance
Repeated comparisons inflate false positives; prespecify outcomes or adjust α
Correlation neither establishes causation nor detects every nonlinear relationship

hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.evidence: Statistical definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

impaired-physician.name: Impaired physician
impaired-physician.scope: Acute impairment, substance use, patient safety protection, physician health programs, mandatory reporting to state medical board
impaired-physician.core: Patient safety first when a colleague's ability to practice safely is compromised.

rows.label: Principle
items: Impairment = functional inability to practice safely from illness, substances, or cognitive decline

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Acute intoxication → stop patient contact, arrange coverage, notify supervisor immediately
★ Document objective observations and affected encounters through institutional channels
★ **Physician health program** → evaluation, treatment, monitoring, and safe return to practice

rows.label: Don't
items: Conceal unsafe care or delay intervention while seeking definitive proof
Permit impaired colleague to drive home

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Report to **state medical board** when law requires or ongoing danger remains unaddressed
PHP confidentiality and reporting exemptions vary by jurisdiction

rows.label: Traps
items: Substance use history or treatment alone ≠ current impairment
Employee assistance referral alone insufficient during an immediate patient safety threat

impaired-physician.evidence: Checked AMA Code of Medical Ethics Opinion 9.3.2.

inflammatory-bowel-disease.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
inflammatory-bowel-disease.scope: Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis, extraintestinal manifestations (erythema nodosum, pyoderma gangrenosum, uveitis), toxic megacolon, colorectal cancer risk, biologic therapy
inflammatory-bowel-disease.core: Chronic relapsing intestinal inflammation: Crohn disease affects any gastrointestinal segment; ulcerative colitis begins in the rectum.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, young adulthood; smoking worsens Crohn disease
NSAIDs and enteric infections can precipitate flares

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss, anemia; children may have growth failure
Arthritis, uveitis; PSC particularly associated with UC
Erythema nodosum: tender nonulcerating nodules; **pyoderma gangrenosum**: rapid painful violaceous ulcer, purulent base
★ Severe colitis: fever, tachycardia, frequent bloody stools; distention, colon >6 cm → **toxic megacolon**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dysregulated mucosal immune response to intestinal microbiota in genetically susceptible hosts

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stool **C. difficile** testing and cultures before attributing worsening diarrhea to inflammation
Fecal calprotectin supports intestinal inflammation; **ileocolonoscopy with biopsies** confirms
Suspected small-bowel disease or abscess → CT/MR enterography; avoid capsule with suspected stricture
Partial SBO, suspected stricture → enterography; older exam questions may expect **water-soluble small-bowel follow-through**
Fulminant colitis → abdominal radiograph and limited sigmoidoscopy; avoid full colonoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute severe UC → hospitalization, **IV methylprednisolone**, fluids, VTE prophylaxis
Steroid-refractory severe UC → infliximab or cyclosporine; perforation or megacolon → urgent colectomy
★ Moderate/severe flare without obstruction or abscess → **prednisone** induces remission only; **never maintenance**
Crohn abscess → antibiotics and drainage before immunosuppression
UC with colorectal cancer → **total proctocolectomy**, not segmental colectomy

rows.label: Complications
items: Fistulas (enterovaginal → vaginal flatus), strictures, obstruction in Crohn; colectomy does not cure Crohn
Terminal ileal Crohn → B12 deficiency, **bile salt malabsorption** → steatorrhea
Colonic disease → colorectal cancer; active inflammation → venous thromboembolism

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Colonic disease → surveillance colonoscopy beginning about **8 years** after onset; PSC → immediately
Vaccinate and screen TB/HBV before biologics; smoking cessation for Crohn

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBS: no bleeding, weight loss or inflammatory markers
Ischemic colitis: abrupt pain followed by hematochezia, vascular risk

table.title: Distribution and outpatient treatment
rows: RLQ mass, cobblestones, perianal disease, granulomas
Bloody diarrhea, tenesmus; friability, crypt abscesses, pseudopolyps

influenza.name: Influenza
influenza.scope: Uncomplicated influenza, high-risk groups, oseltamivir indications, viral pneumonia, secondary bacterial pneumonia, postviral myositis
influenza.core: Abrupt fever, headache, diffuse aches, and dry cough during community circulation; treatment urgency depends on host risk and illness severity.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Droplet/aerosol exposure; crowded settings, incomplete vaccination; influenza A or B
★ High risk: **age <5 or ≥65**, pregnancy/postpartum, immunosuppression, cardiopulmonary/metabolic disease, BMI ≥40
Superinfection: pneumococcus, **Staphylococcus aureus**, Haemophilus influenzae

rows.label: Clues
items: Prominent malaise, chills, sore throat; children may have vomiting/diarrhea
Tachypnea, hypoxemia, hypotension, altered mentation, dehydration → severe/complicated disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Respiratory epithelial infection and cytokine release; impaired mucociliary defenses facilitate bacterial superinfection
Antigenic drift: seasonal variation; influenza A reassortment/shift: pandemic potential

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Molecular NAAT** preferred when testing changes care; hospitalized suspected cases should be tested
Negative rapid antigen test does not exclude infection; clinical diagnosis often sufficient in seasonal uncomplicated illness
Respiratory compromise → pulse oximetry, CXR; bacterial deterioration → cultures when severe

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Oseltamivir**: hospitalized, severe/progressive, or high-risk illness, even >48 h; don't await testing
Otherwise healthy outpatient within 48 h → consider antiviral; mild late presentation → fluids, acetaminophen
Uncomplicated oseltamivir course **5 days**; adjust for renal function; oxygen/IV fluids for physiologic deficits
Pregnancy → oseltamivir preferred; avoid inhaled zanamivir in asthma/COPD; avoid aspirin in children

rows.label: Complications
items: Myocarditis, encephalopathy, rhabdomyolysis, exacerbated chronic disease; aspirin-associated Reye syndrome

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Annual vaccination from 6 months**; inactivated vaccine during pregnancy
First vaccination at age 6 months–8 years may need 2 doses ≥4 weeks apart
Hand hygiene, respiratory precautions; selected high-risk exposures → oseltamivir chemoprophylaxis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Common cold: gradual onset, rhinorrhea predominant, little systemic toxicity
COVID-19: overlapping presentation; multiplex NAAT distinguishes, coinfection possible

table.title: Complication patterns
rows: CAP antibiotics; severe MRSA concern → vancomycin
Child: bilateral calf pain, ↑CK, normal reflexes

influenza.evidence: Checked 2026-11-05: [CDC antivirals, March 2026](https://www.cdc.gov/flu/hcp/antivirals/summary-clinicians.html), [vaccination](https://www.cdc.gov/flu/vaccines/keyfacts.html); established complication patterns.

informed-consent-and-capacity.name: Informed consent and capacity
informed-consent-and-capacity.scope: Decision-making capacity, informed consent, emergency exception (implied consent), refusal of treatment, AMA discharge
informed-consent-and-capacity.core: A capable adult may accept or refuse treatment after understanding its benefits, material risks, alternatives, and consequences of refusal.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ Capacity: **understand, appreciate (own case), reason, communicate**; decision-specific, fluctuating
Competence: legal; diagnosis, age, alcohol use, incarceration, disagreement alone ≠ incapacity

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Explain benefits, material risks, alternatives/no treatment; **qualified interpreter and teach-back**
Correct delirium, intoxication, pain, communication barriers; reassess capacity
AMA request: assess capacity, explore barriers, offer safer plan, document discussion and follow-up

rows.label: Don't
items: Capable refusal → respect choice, even if life-saving or pregnant; avoid coercion, abandonment
No valid consent → possible **battery**; signed form alone insufficient
Refusing one therapy (blood) ≠ refusing all; provide other indicated care, including surgery

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Emergency + incapacity + no surrogate/directive/verified refusal → implied consent to treat
★ Parents refuse minor's life-saving transfusion → **treat emergency**; seek court authority if feasible
Incapacity without emergency → authorized surrogate; involve patient to remaining ability

rows.label: Traps
items: Psychiatric illness does not automatically remove capacity; assess the specific decision
Suicide danger may justify protective detention despite expressed desire to leave
New material procedure or changed risk → renewed consent; consent revocable anytime before procedure

table.title: Who decides
rows: Ask whom to involve; facilitate promptly; no override
Minor decides; no parental consent (state law varies)
Parents seek unproven remedy for child
Continue proven therapy; investigate remedy; CPS not first
Close; discuss after waking; no next-of-kin consent
Autonomy ≠ entitlement; physician refuses, explains, offers alternatives

informed-consent-and-capacity.evidence: Not checked online; established consent/capacity ethics; emergency and minor-consent law varies by jurisdiction.

inherited-bleeding-disorders.name: Inherited bleeding disorders
inherited-bleeding-disorders.scope: Hemophilia A, Hemophilia B, von Willebrand disease, factor XI deficiency, hemarthrosis, mixing studies, factor VIII inhibitors
inherited-bleeding-disorders.core: Deep tissue bleeding suggests a coagulation-factor defect; mucosal bleeding suggests platelet/von Willebrand dysfunction, even with a normal platelet count.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hemophilia A/B: X-linked, usually males; maternal family history may be absent
vWD usually autosomal dominant; factor XI deficiency autosomal, enriched in Ashkenazi ancestry

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Recurrent **hemarthroses**, muscle hematomas and delayed postoperative bleeding → hemophilia
Epistaxis, gingival bleeding, easy bruising and heavy menses → vWD
Factor XI deficiency: variable postsurgical bleeding, especially oral/urologic procedures; hemarthrosis uncommon
Unexpected major bleeding after circumcision or surgery may reveal previously undiagnosed disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: VIII/IX/XI deficits impair intrinsic-pathway thrombin generation and fibrin stabilization
vWF mediates platelet adhesion and stabilizes factor VIII; deficiency impairs primary and sometimes secondary hemostasis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ CBC/platelets, PT, aPTT; **mixing study corrects** factor deficiency, fails with inhibitor
Factor VIII, IX or XI activity identifies deficiency; hemophilia generally normal PT/platelets
★ Suspected vWD → **vWF antigen, activity and factor VIII**; aPTT may be normal
Stress, pregnancy and estrogen raise vWF; repeat borderline testing when clinically stable
Severe hemophilia: factor activity <1%; inhibitor testing if replacement response is inadequate

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Major suspected hemophilic bleeding → **replace deficient factor immediately**, before imaging delays
Hemophilia A → factor VIII; B → factor IX; emicizumab prophylaxis for selected A
Mild responsive A or type 1 vWD → **desmopressin after response testing**
Severe vWD → vWF-containing concentrate; avoid desmopressin in type 2B and ineffective type 3
Mucosal bleeding → tranexamic acid; factor XI procedures → antifibrinolytic ± plasma with hematology planning

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic hemarthropathy, intracranial hemorrhage, anemia; factor inhibitors complicate replacement
Desmopressin → water retention/hyponatremia; factor concentrates can increase thrombosis risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Individualized factor/nonfactor prophylaxis, dental care, procedure planning; avoid aspirin and nonselective NSAIDs
Family genetic counseling; fluid restriction and sodium monitoring around desmopressin

rows.label: Mimics
items: ITP: low platelets with mucocutaneous bleeding
Acquired factor VIII inhibitor: new bleeding, mixing fails to correct
Vitamin K deficiency: PT prolonged first

insomnia.name: Insomnia
insomnia.scope: Chronic insomnia, sleep hygiene, stimulus control therapy, sleep restriction, delayed sleep-wake phase disorder, pharmacotherapy indications
insomnia.core: Persistent difficulty sleeping despite adequate opportunity, with daytime impairment, calls for CBT-I and evaluation of perpetuating causes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Stress, depression/anxiety, chronic pain, irregular schedules, conditioned worry about sleep
Caffeine, alcohol, nicotine, stimulants, glucocorticoids; older age and menopause

rows.label: Clues
items: Difficulty initiating/maintaining sleep or early awakening, fatigue, poor concentration, irritability
★ Chronic disorder: **≥3 nights/week for ≥3 months**, with adequate sleep opportunity
Delayed phase: late sleep/wake times but normal sleep quality and duration when schedule unrestricted
Loud snoring, witnessed apnea, irresistible sleepiness, or restless legs suggests another sleep disorder

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cognitive/physiologic hyperarousal and learned bed–wake association perpetuate insomnia
Circadian phase delay misaligns internal timing with required social schedule

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Sleep history and 1–2-week diary**; review schedule, substances, mood, pain, and medications
Polysomnography: suspected apnea, limb movements, unusual behaviors, or refractory uncertainty; not routine
Actigraphy can clarify circadian timing; assess bipolar disorder before sleep-restriction interventions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **CBT-I first-line**: stimulus control, sleep restriction/compression, cognitive restructuring, relaxation
Stimulus control: bed only for sleep/sex; leave when persistently awake, return when sleepy
Restrict time in bed to consolidate sleep, then expand; fixed wake time and avoid naps
★ **Sleep hygiene alone insufficient**; reduce evening stimulants, alcohol, screens; dark quiet room
Short-term: doxepin, ramelteon, orexin antagonist; acute stressor → **zolpidem**; maintenance + dysphoria → **trazodone**

rows.label: Complications
items: Impaired driving/work, low mood; hypnotics, especially benzodiazepines (alprazolam) → falls, cognitive impairment, dependence
Z-drugs can cause complex sleep behaviors; avoid sedative combinations and routine antihistamines in older adults

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain regular wake time and daytime activity; address pain/mood disorders and relapse triggers
★ Delayed phase → **fixed daily bed and wake times**, morning bright light, evening melatonin, gradual advance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Insufficient sleep: inadequate opportunity, improves with longer sleep duration
Mania: reduced need for sleep with increased energy, rather than distressing fatigue
OSA: sleep fragmentation with snoring/apneas; coexistence possible

interstitial-lung-disease.name: Interstitial lung disease
interstitial-lung-disease.scope: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, sarcoidosis, pneumoconioses, restrictive PFTs (reduced DLCO, normal/high FEV1/FVC), high-resolution CT
interstitial-lung-disease.core: Progressive exertional dyspnea, dry cough, and inspiratory crackles suggest diffuse parenchymal lung disease; HRCT patterns and exposure history identify the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age >60 and smoking: IPF; autoimmune disease; familial fibrosis
Amiodarone, bleomycin, nitrofurantoin; occupational silica/coal/asbestos, organic antigens; prior thoracic radiation

rows.label: Clues
items: Fine basal Velcro crackles, exertional desaturation, later clubbing; systemic rheumatic features can reveal cause
Sarcoidosis: bilateral hilar adenopathy, uveitis, erythema nodosum, sometimes hypercalcemia
Rapidly worsening oxygenation → infection, embolism, edema, or acute exacerbation evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alveolar/interstitial injury and aberrant repair reduce lung compliance and gas-transfer capacity
Granulomatous inflammation or fibrogenic dust responses produce distinct imaging distributions

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **HRCT + full PFTs** after chest radiograph; obtain detailed drug, occupation, hobby, autoimmune history
★ **↓TLC, ↓DLCO, normal/↑FEV1/FVC** support restriction; low FVC alone is insufficient
UIP: basal subpleural reticulation, traction bronchiectasis, honeycombing; exclude known causes before labeling IPF
Autoantibodies when connective-tissue disease suspected; BAL/biopsy selected through multidisciplinary review
Typical UIP without secondary cause may avoid surgical biopsy; assess exertional oxygen needs

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Remove offending exposure/drug**, pulmonary rehabilitation, oxygen for hypoxemia; treat identified cause
★ IPF: **nintedanib or pirfenidone** slows decline; no routine chronic prednisone-based immunosuppression
Inflammatory sarcoid/autoimmune disease: selected steroids or steroid-sparing agents; mild sarcoid may need observation
Progressive fibrotic non-IPF disease → nintedanib consideration; advanced disease → early transplant evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, cor pulmonale, respiratory failure, exacerbations; asbestos raises lung cancer/mesothelioma risk
Silicosis increases TB susceptibility; antifibrotics can cause GI adverse effects and liver injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, respiratory immunizations, occupational dust controls, medication monitoring; follow FVC/DLCO trends

rows.label: Mimics
items: Heart failure: congestion/cardiomegaly, volume response; emphysema: obstruction with hyperinflation
Neuromuscular restriction: low volumes with relatively preserved diffusion capacity

table.title: Imaging clues to etiology
rows: Centrilobular nodules, mosaic attenuation, air trapping

intimate-partner-violence.name: Intimate partner violence
intimate-partner-violence.scope: Screening principles, clinical red flags, pregnancy risk, safety assessment and planning, mandatory reporting distinctions
intimate-partner-violence.core: Privately assess abuse, respect patient autonomy, and connect disclosure to immediate safety assessment and sustained support.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ **Screen reproductive-age women**, including pregnancy/postpartum; assess concerning findings in anyone
Varied-age bruises, delayed care, controlling partner, depression, reproductive coercion → red flags
Pregnancy: abuse may begin or escalate; threatens maternal safety, worsens birth outcomes

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Interview alone**, use professional interpreter; explain confidentiality limits before screening
Validate; document exact words/injuries; assess strangulation, weapons, threats, suicide/homicide risk
★ **Safety plan**: destination, emergency contacts, documents, advocate, ongoing support

rows.label: Don't
items: Avoid partner confrontation, blame, forced departure, or couples counseling during active abuse
Do not leave visible resources or portal messages that could endanger the patient

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ **Reporting laws vary**: check jurisdiction; adult IPV disclosure alone is not universally reportable
Child/elder/dependent-adult abuse, certain injuries → required reports; explain, minimize disclosure

rows.label: Traps
items: Negative screen does not exclude coercion; repeat privately when concern persists
Competent adults retain autonomy absent specific emergency/reporting duty, even when declining police
Screening alone insufficient; multicomponent continuing support provides benefit

intimate-partner-violence.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF IPV recommendation (2025)](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/intimate-partner-violence-and-abuse-of-elderly-and-vulnerable-adults-screening); reporting depends on jurisdiction.

ischemic-stroke-and-tia.name: Ischemic stroke and TIA
ischemic-stroke-and-tia.scope: TIA (including amaurosis fugax), ischemic stroke, acute management (tPA, thrombectomy), secondary prevention, risk factors
ischemic-stroke-and-tia.core: Abrupt focal neurologic loss from cerebral ischemia; transient monocular blindness means retinal embolism from the ipsilateral carotid.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Hypertension: greatest modifiable risk factor**; smoking, diabetes, dyslipidemia, carotid atherosclerosis
Atrial fibrillation, recent MI, endocarditis, arterial dissection

rows.label: Clues
items: **Broca** nonfluent, poor repetition, intact comprehension; **Wernicke** fluent paraphasias, poor comprehension, no insight
Crossed: **Weber** ipsilateral CN III, contralateral hemiparesis (midbrain); lateral pons: ipsilateral full-face palsy, deafness
★ **Last known well** establishes treatment timing; symptom discovery time may differ
TIA: resolved deficit without acute infarction, often embolic; urgent evaluation despite normal examination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Thromboembolism or small-vessel occlusion → infarct core surrounded by salvageable penumbra
Reperfusion preserves threatened tissue but increases hemorrhagic transformation risk

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Fingerstick glucose + **noncontrast head CT** first; normal early CT does not exclude ischemia
CTA head/neck for large-vessel occlusion; MRI diffusion for small infarcts or diagnostic uncertainty
ECG, telemetry, carotid imaging; echocardiography for suspected cardiac emboli

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Disabling deficit, eligible ≤4.5 hours → **alteplase or tenecteplase**; imaging-selected extended windows possible
Thrombolysis: BP <185/110 before, <180/105 after; exclude bleeding and significant anticoagulant effect
★ Large-vessel occlusion → **mechanical thrombectomy**, selected cases through 24 hours; do not delay thrombolysis
No reperfusion: generally allow BP ≤220/120; oxygen for hypoxemia; swallow assessment before oral intake
Aspirin after hemorrhage excluded; after thrombolysis, wait 24 hours and repeat imaging

rows.label: Complications
items: Cerebral edema, aspiration, venous thrombosis, seizures, disability

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Minor noncardioembolic stroke/high-risk TIA → short **aspirin + clopidogrel**, then single antiplatelet
AF/cardioembolic → oral anticoagulation, timing by infarct/bleeding risk; noncardioembolic → antiplatelet only
Symptomatic carotid stenosis 70–99% → endarterectomy when eligible; selected 50–69% also benefit
Long-term antiplatelet (aspirin allergy → clopidogrel); undertreated hypertension → **intensify antihypertensives**; high-intensity statin

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypoglycemia: deficit reverses with glucose
Migraine aura: spreading positive symptoms; seizure: witnessed convulsion followed by Todd paralysis

table.title: Vascular localization
rows: Occipital: contralateral homonymous hemianopia; macular sparing
Diplopia, vertigo, dysarthria, ataxia, crossed/bilateral signs, coma
Vertigo; ipsilateral Horner/face/ataxia/palate; contralateral body pain-temperature

learning-disorders.name: Learning disorders
learning-disorders.scope: Specific learning disorder with impairment in reading (dyslexia), written expression (dysgraphia), mathematics (dyscalculia), individualized education plan (IEP)
learning-disorders.core: Persistent difficulty acquiring specific academic skills despite targeted instruction, with impairment exceeding that explained by intellectual, sensory, or educational factors.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, prematurity, developmental language disorder
ADHD frequently coexists; bilingualism or socioeconomic disadvantage alone does not establish a disorder

rows.label: Clues
items: Academic difficulty disproportionate to functioning in other domains; frustration, avoidance, low confidence
Onset during school years; deficits may emerge only when demands exceed compensatory strategies
★ Reading difficulty reflects phonologic processing, **not simply reversing letters**
Persistent effort without expected skill acquisition distinguishes disability from occasional poor performance

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Neurodevelopmental differences in domain-specific information processing; unrelated to laziness
Skills improve with intervention, but underlying vulnerability often persists into adulthood

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Difficulties **≥6 months despite targeted support** + substantially below-age academic achievement
Individual standardized achievement testing + developmental, educational, and psychosocial history
★ Assess **hearing and vision**; evaluate language, attention, attendance, and quality of instruction
IQ–achievement discrepancy not required; global cognitive/adaptive deficits suggest intellectual disability instead
Evaluate each affected domain; multiple impairment specifiers may apply

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ School evaluation → **IEP** with explicit specialized instruction, measurable goals, periodic progress review
Reading: systematic phonics/phonemic-awareness instruction; writing/math: structured domain-specific teaching
Accommodations: extended time, assistive technology, reduced distraction; 504 plan when access accommodations suffice
Treat comorbid ADHD when present; stimulants do not directly remediate academic skill deficits

rows.label: Complications
items: School avoidance, dropout, anxiety/depression, reduced self-esteem
Unrecognized difficulties may be mislabeled as defiance or poor motivation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early developmental/literacy surveillance and prompt intervention reduce secondary academic and emotional harm
Coordinate family, school, and clinicians; reinforce strengths and protect against bullying

rows.label: Mimics
items: Intellectual disability: broad intellectual and adaptive impairments
ADHD: pervasive inattention across settings; skill deficits may coexist
Inadequate schooling: insufficient instruction or limited language exposure explains performance

table.title: Academic domains
rows: Spelling, grammar, organization of written ideas

learning-disorders.evidence: Not checked against a current guideline online; established DSM-based educational and pediatric teaching.

low-back-pain.name: Low back pain
low-back-pain.scope: Lumbosacral strain, herniated disk and radiculopathy, spinal stenosis, red flags, imaging indications, conservative management
low-back-pain.core: Most acute low back pain improves with activity and analgesia; neurologic deficits or systemic red flags change the workup.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Heavy lifting, deconditioning, obesity, prolonged sitting
Cancer, immunosuppression, injection drug use, osteoporosis, chronic glucocorticoids increase serious-pathology risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Mechanical pain varies with movement; isolated axial pain without systemic illness favors benign disease
★ **Urinary retention, saddle anesthesia, bilateral weakness** → cauda equina emergency
Fever, weight loss, night pain, trauma, or progressive weakness → targeted urgent evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Paraspinal injury causes localized pain; degenerative narrowing or disk extrusion compresses neural structures

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ No red flags → **no initial imaging**, including routine radiographs
Focused strength, reflex, sensory, gait examination; straight-leg raise supports lower lumbar radiculopathy
★ Suspected infection, malignancy, cord compression → **MRI**; suspected fracture → radiograph or CT
Persistent symptoms despite about 6 weeks' care → MRI if intervention being considered
Suspected spinal infection → ESR/CRP, blood cultures; normal temperature does not exclude infection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Continue activity**, no heavy lifting until pain resolves, heat, short NSAID course; avoid prolonged bed rest
Physical therapy if pain persists despite NSAIDs; avoid routine opioids and systemic steroids
Progressive motor deficit or cauda equina → urgent surgical decompression
Refractory disabling radicular pain → epidural injection or diskectomy after imaging correlation

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic pain, functional limitation, medication dependence
Untreated compression → permanent bladder, bowel, sexual, or motor dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: Core strengthening, regular exercise, ergonomic lifting, weight management

rows.label: Mimics
items: AAA: abdominal pulsatile mass, vascular risk, hypotension
Renal colic: flank-to-groin pain, hematuria; inflammatory back pain: improves with exercise
Vascular claudication: calf pain, bicycling too; standing still relieves; weak pulses alone don't exclude stenosis

table.title: Mechanical patterns
rows: Leg pain below knee; cough aggravates
Shopping-cart sign; pulses usually preserved; MRI confirms

low-back-pain.evidence: Not checked online; established generalist back-pain evaluation.

lymphoma.name: Lymphoma
lymphoma.scope: Hodgkin lymphoma (Reed-Sternberg cells, CD15/CD30, B symptoms, mediastinal mass), non-Hodgkin lymphoma (diffuse large B-cell, follicular, Burkitt, mantle cell), Ann Arbor staging, excisional lymph node biopsy
lymphoma.core: Persistent painless lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, or constitutional symptoms require tissue diagnosis; lymphoma subtype determines urgency, staging, and treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: EBV, HIV, transplantation/immunosuppression; autoimmune disease and older age for many NHL subtypes
Hodgkin incidence peaks in young adults and older age

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **B symptoms**: unexplained fever >38 °C, drenching night sweats, >10% weight loss in 6 months
Young adult, persistent painless cervical node + **generalized pruritus** → suspect Hodgkin
Rubbery nodes; NHL often noncontiguous/extranodal
Rapidly enlarging mass, cytopenias, high LDH → aggressive disease; mediastinal disease may obstruct airway/SVC

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Clonal lymphocyte proliferation; most NHLs are B-cell derived
Classical Hodgkin: sparse malignant cells within a reactive inflammatory background

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Excisional lymph-node biopsy** preserves architecture; core if excision unsafe; FNA alone generally insufficient
Histology, immunophenotyping/flow cytometry, selected cytogenetics classify disease; PET/CT stages FDG-avid lymphoma
Ann Arbor: I one region; II same diaphragm side; III both sides; IV disseminated extranodal disease
CBC, CMP, LDH, uric acid; HIV/HBV/HCV testing before systemic treatment
Stable before biopsy → avoid glucocorticoids obscuring histology; life-threatening compression → urgent specialist management

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early classical HL → **ABVD ± involved-site radiation**; advanced disease → nivolumab-AVD among current options
DLBCL → rituximab-based combination, commonly R-CHOP; Burkitt → urgent intensive chemotherapy with CNS-directed treatment
Asymptomatic low-burden follicular disease → observation; symptomatic/bulky disease → anti-CD20-based treatment
★ Assess tumor-lysis risk before cytotoxic treatment; hydration and **urate-lowering prophylaxis** when risk warrants

rows.label: Complications
items: Tumor lysis, marrow failure, infection, cord compression, superior vena cava syndrome
Doxorubicin → cardiomyopathy; bleomycin → lung toxicity; later infertility/secondary cancers

rows.label: Prevention
items: Anti-CD20 plus HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ → entecavir/tenofovir prophylaxis; fertility preservation before chemotherapy
Survivorship care: cardiovascular risk, thyroid/breast surveillance after relevant radiation exposures

rows.label: Mimics
items: Reactive nodes: tender, infection-linked, regress after illness
TB lymphadenitis: granulomatous inflammation; microbiologic confirmation
Leukemia: circulating blasts or marked blood-count abnormalities; marrow evaluation

measures-of-association.name: Measures of association
measures-of-association.scope: Relative risk (RR), odds ratio (OR), attributable risk (AR), absolute risk reduction (ARR), number needed to treat (NNT), number needed to harm (NNH), hazard ratio
measures-of-association.core: Relative measures describe proportional associations; absolute measures incorporate baseline risk and determine treatment benefit or harm.

rows.label: Definition
items: CER = control event rate; EER = experimental event rate
Two-by-two table: exposed events/non-events a/b; unexposed events/non-events c/d
Relative risk reduction (RRR; vaccine efficacy) = (CER − EER)/CER = 1 − RR

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ Ratio null = **1**; risk-difference null = **0**
★ Hazard ratio compares instantaneous event rates over time; not cumulative risk ratio
NNT/NNH require specified outcome and follow-up duration; always round up

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ RR: cohort/RCT; OR: case-control and logistic regression
